[Source 1 — www.pravda.com.ua] (URL: https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/10/09/8057184/):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
UP journalist Tkach released but still out of contact, cameraman Bondarenko injured – editor-in-chief

Ukrainska Pravda Editor-in-Chief Sevğil Musaieva has reported that Mykhailo Tkach, head of UP's investigative journalism department, has been released after being detained in Vienna. However, the editorial team is still unable to contact him, while cameraman Yaroslav Bondarenko was injured during the detention.

Actual Article Body:
Долучайтеся до клубу УП!

Ukrainska Pravda Editor-in-Chief Sevğil Musaieva has reported that Mykhailo Tkach, head of UP's investigative journalism department, has been released after being detained in Vienna. However, the editorial team is still unable to contact him, while cameraman Yaroslav Bondarenko was injured during the detention.

Source: Sevğil Musaieva on Facebook

Quote: "At 04:00 on 9 October… Mykhailo Tkach was released after being detained in Vienna for more than 12 hours. However, his communication devices have still not been returned to him, so the editorial team is currently unable to contact him directly. Our colleague Yaroslav Bondarenko was injured during the detention and was taken to hospital. The police only began questioning him during the night."

Details: The editorial team does not currently know the procedural status of either journalist.

"The allegations made against our colleagues while they were being held are unlike anything the editorial team has encountered before and raise serious questions. We expect the Austrian law enforcement authorities to explain the circumstances surrounding the detention of our colleagues, Yaroslav's injury and the reasons why they were both held for such a long time. We also expect clarification of their procedural status and the return of their communication devices," Musaieva said.

She recalled that Tkach had previously been detained while carrying out journalistic assignments in various countries, but in those cases he had been released within an hour and a half to two hours after the circumstances had been clarified.

"This is the first time our colleagues have been held for more than 12 hours. The length of the detention, the nature of the allegations made against our colleagues, Yaroslav's injury and the lack of direct contact with Mykhailo are causing us serious concern," Musaieva concluded.

Previously: Earlier this morning, Ukraine's Foreign Ministry reported that Ukrainska Pravda journalist Mykhailo Tkach, who had been detained in Vienna the previous day, had been released.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Ukrainian grandmother released after Russia had her arrested in Kazakhstan on kidnapping charges. She’d traveled there to retrieve her grandson. — Meduza

Liubov Rozhanska, a Ukrainian citizen detained in Kazakhstan at Russia’s request, has been released, her lawyer, Alexei Pryanishnikov, told Vot Tak.

Actual Article Body:
Liubov Rozhanska, a Ukrainian citizen detained in Kazakhstan at Russia’s request, has been released, her lawyer, Alexei Pryanishnikov, told Vot Tak.

“The detention period had expired. Since no pretrial restriction had been assigned, she was released from the detention facility,” he said.

He said Rozhanska was released as early as October 4. She then spent several days on the grounds of the Ukrainian embassy before leaving Kazakhstan for Odesa.

Rozhanska had flown to Kazakhstan from Istanbul in early October to pick up her grandson, who was to be brought from Russia. The boy’s mother had taken him from Ukraine to Russia in 2021.

According to Pryanishnikov, the boy’s father had allowed only a temporary trip, but the boy and his mother never returned to Ukraine and instead obtained Russian citizenship. Ukrainian courts, including Ukraine’s Supreme Court, ruled that the boy should live with his father.

Relatives of the boy’s mother contacted Rozhanska and offered to hand the boy over to her in Kazakhstan. At the same time, Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) directorate in the Kaliningrad region, where the mother and boy live, had petitioned a court for an arrest warrant against Rozhanska on charges of attempted kidnapping. When Rozhanska flew to Astana from Istanbul, she was detained at the airport at Russia’s request.

Rozhanska’s lawyer insists that his client was carrying out the ruling of Ukrainian courts that determined the boy should live with his father.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
DHS chief Mullin says NY ignored nearly 15K detainer requests for illegal immigrant criminals: ‘Absolute silence’

"Silence. Absolute silence is what we've got from New York off of those retainers," Mullin told reporters at DHS headquarters.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

WASHINGTON — Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin revealed Friday that New York state officials have refused to honor a single detainer request from his department for illegal immigrants in their custody, many of whom had “extensive criminal backgrounds.”

The Department of Homeland Security has issued 14,766 detainers to New York law enforcement entities, Mullin noted, for migrants accused of a total of 47,750 felony charges.

“Silence. Absolute silence is what we’ve got from New York off of those retainers,” Mullin told reporters at DHS headquarters.

“So you have to ask yourself, why would they release these individuals back onto the streets? They’re illegals,” he added. “They have no right to be back into the United States. They’ve committed a crime. We know that they’re the worst, the worst.”

The comments came hours after an Immigration and Customs Enforcement-involved shooting in the Bronx of a suspected gang member, 28-year-old Oscar Belgal, while a 5-year-old boy believed to be his son sat in the back of his SUV.
